request: Analyze GSE145263 for PMID 33661096 (Cardiovascular disease risk factors induce mesenchymal features and senescence in mouse cardiac endothelial cells.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (SMARTer Stranded Total RNA-Seq Pico v2) of FACS-sorted cardiac endothelial cells (CD31+CD140a-CD45-Ter119-DAPI-), NextSeq 550 single-end
final.primary_estimand: Effect of 6-week progressive treadmill exercise training vs sedentary on the cardiac endothelial-cell transcriptome in young adult (10-week-old at start) male C57BL/6J mice
planned_contrasts: EXE vs SED (S2.1.p1, FIG2A; DEG count shown only in the MA-plot image, not in text)
final.other_experiments_in_series: Aged vs Young, HFD vs Chow, TAC 2wk vs Sham, TAC 7wk vs Sham (each with its own control; not exercise; out of scope)
final.sample_inclusion: SED1-3 (n=3) and EXE1-3 (n=3) male mice; FIG2 legend N=3-4 male mice/group
final.repeated_measure_unit: none (independent animals, one EC sample per mouse)
final.normalization: DESeq2 size factors on HTSeq raw counts (S4.15.p1)
final.paper_method: DESeq2 (Chipster v3.12.2) two-group, ~ group, Wald test, BH FDR (S4.15.p1)
final.paper_results: Exercise affected fewer genes than the risk factors (S2.1.p2, S3.p2). Serpinh1, Vwa1, Mest and Fhl3 significantly DOWN-regulated by exercise (S2.3.p1, FIG4A-C). PANTHER ORA of up/down genes (S2.2.p1, S4.16.p1).

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S2.1.p1 defines exercise training (6 wk treadmill) vs sedentary as one of five experiments; S4.2.p1: 10-wk-old male mice used for RNA-seq; S4.15.p1: HTSeq counts -> DESeq2 Wald + BH, FDR <= 0.05; FIG2 legend: FDR (BH) threshold 0.05, n=3-4/group. No fold-change cutoff is stated. The exercise DEG count appears only inside the FIG2A image, which is not in the text, so no numeric paper count is available.

checks: GEO titles SED1-3/EXE1-3 with treatment Sedentary/Exercise training match the paper's groups
data_processing: HISAT2 GRCm38.90 + HTSeq-count, as in S4.15.p1

ownership.reasoning: Series is the paper's own deposit (S11.p1, S11.p3; same authors Kivela and Hemanthakumar). Per-sample HTSeq count files in GSE145263_RAW.tar are the only matrix.

alignment.reasoning: Tar-merged columns are GSM ids that equal the metadata index exactly (31/31). Group column 'grp' is derived by recoding the GEO treatment characteristic. The 25 samples of the aging/HFD/TAC experiments are excluded because the paper compares each intervention only with its own control; using them would change the estimand.

matrix.reasoning: All values are integers (integer_fraction 1.0, max 5.4M, many zeros); GEO data_processing and S4.15.p1 state HTSeq-count read counts per gene; paper used these raw counts as DESeq2 input. No HTSeq '__' summary rows remain in the merged matrix.

candidates.value: one model over all 31 samples with every group as a level
candidates.reason_rejected: paper fits each experiment separately against its own control (S2.1.p1, FIG2A-E); pooling unrelated experiments changes the dispersion estimates and the estimand

design.reasoning: Independent-group comparison of trained vs sedentary male mice, n=3 vs 3, exactly as FIG2A. Causal estimand (randomised intervention vs sedentary control).

covariance.reasoning: One sample per animal, no pairing or batch variable recorded for the SED/EXE samples (all submitted Feb 13 2020; the Sep 2020 additions belong to other experiments and are excluded). All male. No covariate is added.

deviations: pydeseq2 implementation instead of R DESeq2 in Chipster; same model (NB GLM, empirical-Bayes dispersion shrinkage, Wald test, BH). Small numerical differences expected, especially from independent filtering and outlier handling.

method.reasoning: Raw counts support DESeq2, the paper's method (S4.15.p1).

threshold.reasoning: S4.15.p1: FDR (p adj.) <= 0.05; FIG2 legend: BH-adjusted p threshold 0.05; no fold-change rule. Audit adds |log2FC| > 1 for reference only.

caveats: Paper's exercise DEG count is only in the FIG2A image and could not be read; no numeric count comparison.
n=3 per group; results are sensitive to single animals.
